paragraphs: Issur the convert. At his death, before Rava, he gave his son Rav Mari—who was not then in the same place as his father Issur the convert—thirteen thousand zuz through acknowledgment, since a convert does not inherit his father. See Bava Batra 149a: Issur the convert had twelve thousand zuz with Rava. His son Rav Mari was conceived before conversion and born after conversion. (He had relations with Rachel, Mar Shmuel’s daughter, before converting; she conceived Rav Mari bar Rachel, and meanwhile he converted and Rav Mari was born. She was among Shmuel’s daughters taken captive, as in Ketubbot—Rashbam.) He was at the academy. Rava said, “How can Rav Mari acquire these coins? By inheritance—he is no heir. By gift—a deathbed gift is like inheritance.” (Thus I acquire them: a convert’s property is ownerless, in my hands, and I have priority in acquiring it.) Issur acknowledged the coins belonged to his son Rav Mari, as they instructed him to do, and Rava took offense, etc. Tosafot, Kiddushin 18a, ask how Rava wanted to acquire them, since his birth was after conversion. Avodah Zarah, Hashokher 70a: he told Rava that, as a gentile, he had thought Israelites did not keep Shabbat, since if they found a purse of dinars they would take it. He did not know one could carry it in stages of less than four cubits. He entered a business arrangement with Rav Safra, and they came before Rabbah bar Rav Huna, Bava Metzia 31, end of b. He was a sage; his sons and sons’ sons were amoraim. (See Rav Acha the elder.)
